requirements.quote: A lane whose prompt is 40 KB runs on Windows
The unit test for the argv/stdin decision covers win32

Make the threshold platform-aware: on `win32` use stdin for any prompt above a conservative limit (e.g. 16 KiB), or always use stdin on Windows since `claude --print` reads it when no prompt argument is given.
Count the full command line (system-prompt file path, flags), not only the prompt.

deliverables.change: Add CLI_ARGV_PROMPT_MAX_BYTES_WIN32 (16 KiB) and a small pure helper promptGoesViaStdin(prompt, otherArgs, platform) choosing limit by platform and counting prompt bytes plus other argv bytes; use it at the promptViaStdin decision (~:1597), computing the non-prompt args first. Net growth under 150 lines; stdin delivery (:1653) unchanged.
Extend the #4129 argv/stdin test (~:4238) with win32 cases: 40 KB prompt goes to stdin, 10 KB stays argv, long other args tip a borderline prompt to stdin; linux behaviour unchanged.

preserve.what: Linux/macOS behaviour: prompts <=64 KiB stay in argv, larger go over stdin (bin/runner.mjs runCliBackend, runCliBackendAsync).
Existing export list tested at bin/tests/runner.test.mjs:7 and CLI_ARGV_PROMPT_MAX_BYTES export used by bin/lean/lean.test.mjs:4239.
DETERMINISTIC_SPAWN_ERRNOS and stdin delivery via spawn input (bin/runner.mjs:1541,1653).

decisions.choice: Keep the helper in bin/runner.mjs rather than a new file
decisions.justification: A new file under bin would join the enumerated file list at bin/lean/lean.test.mjs:66; the helper is ~10 lines, far below the 150-line hotspot growth limit.
